decisive_items: Methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures associated with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching.
Chest CT (lung window) showed cavitary and noncavitary nodules and masses with faint surrounding ground-glass opacity (“halo sign”)
Histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and fungal elements.
response.rationale: Septate hyphae with acute-angle branching in a necrotizing pulmonary granuloma and halo-sign cavitary nodules are characteristic of invasive pulmonary aspergillosis. R1 is the same entity; R5 is preferred for its explicit pulmonary-site qualifier. Histoplasma and Cryptococcus would appear as yeasts, and Mucor has broad nonseptate right-angle hyphae.

rejected.why: Histoplasmosis manifests as small intracellular yeast rather than septate acute-angle-branching hyphae, and the CT pattern is not chronic fibrocavitary histoplasmosis.
General histoplasmosis also requires yeast forms on silver stain, not the septate acute-angle-branching hyphae described.
Mucormycosis is characterized by broad, pauciseptate hyphae with right-angle branching, directly contradicted by acute-angle septate hyphae.
Cryptococcosis appears as encapsulated yeast with narrow budding, not septate hyphae with acute-angle branching.
